issues.description: The problem statement and UML require Farm.animals to be a List<Animal> and explicitly instruct students to implement it using an ArrayList (problem_statement.md). The template Farm.java contains a placeholder expecting that structure, but the provided solution implements the collection as a Queue<Animal> backed by a LinkedList. This divergence (List/ArrayList vs Queue/LinkedList) is a structural mismatch that can confuse students about the expected type for the animals attribute and the required getter/setter signatures and may cause tests or instructions that expect a List/ArrayList to fail or be unclear.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the solution (and template guidance) with the problem statement: use a List<Animal> as the field type and instantiate it as a new ArrayList<>() in the no-argument constructor. Update getter and setter signatures to return/accept List<Animal>. Alternatively, update the problem statement and UML to explicitly allow a Queue/LinkedList if that was the intended type, and adjust instructions and tests accordingly.

issues.description: The problem statement specifically requires the Farm's collection of animals to be a List implemented with an ArrayList, but the solution's Farm uses a Queue backed by a LinkedList (identifier names: Queue/LinkedList vs List/ArrayList). The template Farm is also missing the animals attribute (TODO) so students may expect to find or implement an ArrayList based on the instructions. This mismatch in the collection type name and implementation can create unnecessary confusion when students map the problem requirements to the provided code and solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the collection type consistent across artifacts. Either update the solution (and template) to use List<Animal> animals = new ArrayList<>() as stated in the problem, or relax/update the problem text/UML to state that any List/Queue implementation is acceptable (e.g., use the interface name Collection/Queue and avoid explicitly requiring ArrayList). Preferably change the solution's field to 'private List<Animal> animals;' and initialize it with 'new ArrayList<>()' to match the exercise instructions.
